summary_paragraph: A 68-year-old female with end-stage renal disease, diastolic heart failure, and atrial fibrillation was admitted after developing acute dyspnea and palpitations when lying down, following a recent hospitalization for post-dialysis hypotension. She presented with severe hypertension and hypoxia, requiring BiPAP and intravenous nitroglycerin. Imaging revealed pulmonary edema and right-sided lung consolidation, initially concerning for pneumonia, but clinical improvement favored heart failure as the primary cause. She was restarted on antihypertensive therapy with metoprolol, lisinopril, and valsartan, held on dialysis days to prevent hypotension. A urine culture grew Klebsiella pneumoniae, prompting treatment with Bactrim dosed around dialysis. Her INR rose to 4.0 due to drug interaction, leading to temporary discontinuation of warfarin. She also reported left eye pain from glaucoma, managed with analgesia and continued eye drops. After two dialysis sessions and clinical stabilization, she was discharged home in good condition, breathing comfortably on room air with controlled blood pressure and instructions for close follow-up.
problems: Acute on chronic diastolic heart failure
Hypertensive chronic kidney disease, malignant, with chronic kidney disease stage V or end stage renal disease
Urinary tract infection, site not specified
